title: Quarterly commitment heatmap & stakeholder pact for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Synthesize cross-functional commitments for the next quarter by producing a commitment heatmap and a lightweight stakeholder pact that binds product, engineering, reliability, and GTM on what hosted API model lineup and runway will be delivered, what fallbacks are acceptable, and how capacity hedges are funded. This ticket scopes the planning artifact, stakeholder review cadence, acceptance criteria, and handoff mechanics to execution cycles. The goal is to reduce misalignment scenarios that previously caused unplanned model rollbacks and capacity overruns during seasonal demand spikes.
goals: Produce a visual commitment heatmap mapping feature/endpoint/model variants to commitment lanes and confidence bands
Agree an explicit stakeholder pact (owners, SLAs, contingency funds) for model rotations and emergency fallback triggers
Surface capacity hedges required for the committed runway and assign funding/engineering owners
Define an execution handoff checklist for canaries, rollouts, and post-rollout evals tied to monitoring signals
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap artifact published to Confluence with per-endpoint commitment lane (Green/Amber/Red) and rationale
Stakeholder pact signed by leads from Product, Eng (Serving + Infra), Reliability, and Solutions Eng
Capacity hedge plan with cost estimates and named approvers uploaded to Finance/Capacity board
Rollout playbook updated with explicit canary windows, rollback triggers, and post-canary eval checklist
All listed dependencies have owners and estimated delivery dates in Linear
notes_and_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Eng (Eva Ross), Reliability (Marcus Li), and Solutions Eng (Priya Desai). Agreed scope and initial list of endpoints prioritized for Q2.

2026-03-04: Draft heatmap template created; focusing on high-throughput endpoints (text-generation-chat, embeddings, reranking). Initial confidence bands set using last quarter's latency & token-cost variance.

2026-03-06: Decision: prefer 'capacity hedge' via dedicated burst pool vs. spot scaling. Trade-off logged: burst pool increases committed spend but reduces risk of cross-tenant noisy neighbor events. TODO: Finance to approve hedge budget.
2026-03-08: Design review feedback from UX (Maya Kim): heatmap must include 'customer facing SLA' overlay for enterprise endpoints. Added as follow-up.
2026-03-09: PM/Eng alignment: add mandatory post-rollout evals (quality regression checks on 5 canonical prompt sets) for any model swap to medium+ risk endpoints.
2026-03-10: Pact draft circulated to exec sponsors. Requested red-line changes from Legal around notification windows for customers — legal review scheduled 2026-03-12.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Unexpected model quality regressions during swap. Mitigation: require gated evals and automatic rollback on degradation thresholds
Risk: Capacity costs exceed approved budget. Mitigation: pre-approve a minimal burst pool and conditional additional funding tied to clearly defined traffic signals
Risk: Stakeholder sign-off delays. Mitigation: synchronous review windows and an escalation path to VP-level sponsors with a 48-hour decision SLA
next_steps: Complete capacity hedge cost estimate (owner: Finance -> Anika Bose) by 2026-03-19
Legal review of customer notification window (owner: Legal -> Daniel Hart) by 2026-03-12
Stakeholder pact sign-off meeting scheduled for 2026-03-22
